tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q1 fiscal 2025 growth drivers AI demand

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q1 fiscal 2025 growth drivers AI demand

NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue reached a record **$22.6 billion in Q1 fiscal 2025** (quarter ended April 28, 2024), rising **23% sequentially** from Q4 FY2024 and **427% year over year**; it represented roughly **87%** of the company’s $26.0 billion quarterly revenue. [[1]]

**Primary growth driver: Hopper-based generative-AI compute.** NVIDIA attributed the expansion to “strong and accelerating” demand for generative-AI **training and inference** running on its Hopper platform, which included products such as H100 GPUs and Grace Hopper systems. [[1]]

**Demand broadened beyond hyperscalers.** Cloud-service providers remained important customers, but NVIDIA said generative-AI spending had expanded into consumer-internet companies, enterprises, sovereign-AI projects, automotive, and healthcare—creating several multibillion-dollar end markets rather than relying solely on a narrow group of cloud buyers. [[1]]

**AI-infrastructure buildout supported system-level sales.** NVIDIA highlighted new AI-networking offerings—Quantum and Spectrum-X800 switches—optimized for trillion-parameter GPU computing, as well as expanded AI collaborations with AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft, and Oracle. [[1]]

**Enterprise inference was becoming an additional catalyst.** The launch of NVIDIA AI Enterprise 5.0 and NIM inference microservices was intended to accelerate enterprise generative-AI application development, extending demand from model training into deploying and serving models. [[1]] 

In short, the extraordinary Q1 FY2025 Data Center growth reflected a supply-backed ramp in Hopper AI systems and an unusually broad AI-capex cycle spanning hyperscale cloud, internet platforms, enterprise deployments, sovereign infrastructure, and industry-specific customers. [[1]]

Sources:
[S5.1] NVIDIA Corporation - NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2025 — https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2024/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2025/default.aspx

source_references.title: NVIDIA Corporation - NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2025

tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q2 fiscal 2025 growth drivers AI demand

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q2 fiscal 2025 growth drivers AI demand

NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was **$26.3 billion in Q2 FY2025** (quarter ended July 28, 2024), representing **16% sequential growth** and **154% year-over-year growth**; it accounted for approximately **87.5%** of the company’s $30.0 billion total revenue. [[1]] 

The principal driver was exceptionally strong demand for NVIDIA’s **Hopper GPU computing platform and associated networking**, as customers continued to build and modernize AI infrastructure for generative-AI workloads. [[2]] [[1]] 

Demand was broad-based across **frontier-model developers, consumer-internet companies, and enterprises deploying generative-AI applications**, rather than originating from only one customer class. [[2]] 

At the workload level, NVIDIA identified generative-AI **model training and inference** as key contributors, alongside CUDA-enabled data preprocessing and post-processing for video, images and text, synthetic-data generation, AI recommendation systems, and SQL/vector-database processing. [[2]] 

The growth also reflected expanding sales of **networking** products: compute revenue rose more than 2.5x year over year, networking revenue more than doubled, and Ethernet-for-AI revenue doubled sequentially as hundreds of customers adopted NVIDIA Ethernet offerings. [[2]] 

Product-cycle dynamics further supported demand: the **H200 platform began ramping** during Q2 with large cloud service providers, customers were accelerating Hopper purchases while preparing to adopt Blackwell, and NVIDIA said Hopper demand remained strong with Blackwell demand anticipated to exceed supply. [[2]] 

In short, the 154% increase was driven by hyperscale and broader enterprise AI-capex demand for Hopper-based accelerated computing and networking, expanding inference as well as training workloads, and customers positioning capacity for the subsequent Blackwell platform transition. [[2]] [[1]]

Sources:
[S6.1] NVIDIA Corporation - NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2025 — https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2024/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-2025/default.aspx
[S6.2] Investor Presentation Q2 FY25 September 3, 2024 — https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2025/q2/NVDA-F2Q25-Quarterly-Presentation-FINAL.pdf

In short, the extraordinary Q1 FY2025 Data Center growth reflected a supply-backed ramp in Hopper AI systems and an unusually broad AI-capex cycle spanning hyperscale cloud, internet platforms, enterprise deployments, sovereign infrastructure, and industry-specific customers. [[1]]
